classification.difficultyReason: Convert the stated radius-to-diameter relationship into an area ratio, subtract the inner circle, and combine the ring's fraction of the outer circle with the three shaded sectors out of six.

content.prompt:
The diagram shows two circles with the same centre.
The radius of the outer circle is equal to the diameter of the inner circle.
If the region between the two circles is divided into six equal segments, what fraction of the area of the outer circle is shaded in the diagram?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 11, concentric-circle diagram below the prompt on the left
spec.description: Two concentric circles with six equal annular sectors. The upper-left, right and lower-left sectors are shaded. The inner disc remains white; no centre marker, dimensions or labels are printed.
spec.mathematics: The outer radius is twice the inner radius. Annular boundaries occur at 30, 90, 150, 210, 270 and 330 degrees. Three of the six annular sectors are shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: The shaded regions are permanent question givens. No supplied answer or solution annotation appears in the diagram.

answer.short: $\frac{3}{8}$. Half the ring is shaded, and the ring occupies $\frac{3}{4}$ of the outer circle.
answer.worked:
Let the inner radius be $r$, so the outer radius is $2r$.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{ring}} &= \pi(2r)^2-\pi r^2 \\
A_{\text{ring}} &= 3\pi r^2
\end{align*}$$
Three of the six equal sectors are shaded, so half the ring is shaded.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\text{shaded}} &= \frac{1}{2}\times3\pi r^2 \\
\text{Fraction shaded} &= \frac{\frac{3}{2}\pi r^2}{\pi(2r)^2} \\
\text{Fraction shaded} &= \frac{3}{8}
\end{align*}$$
